description: Ingredient-function map. Obligations are tagged by what an ingredient does, not only its name, so a ban on a function (for example synthetic color) resolves to every affected product in one query even when statutes name ingredients individually.

functions.label: Color
functions.definition: Adds or modifies color. Synthetic FD&C dyes are the most heavily targeted function across both federal phase-out and state school-food bans.

functions.label: Sweetener
functions.definition: Provides sweetness, caloric or non-nutritive. Added sugar drives front-of-package and SNAP exposure; non-nutritive sweeteners drive UPF definitions and labeling challenges.

functions.label: Preservative
functions.definition: Extends shelf life or prevents spoilage. Early GRAS re-review targets sit here.

functions.label: Emulsifier
functions.definition: Keeps otherwise separating components mixed. Relevant to flavored and citrus beverages.

functions.label: Flavor
functions.definition: Provides or modifies taste and aroma. Some flavor carriers and components appear on state target lists.

functions.label: Stimulant
functions.definition: Provides a functional stimulant effect. Drives caffeine labeling and supplemented-foods caution requirements.

functions.label: Contaminant
functions.definition: Not added intentionally but present as a trace. Drives Proposition 65 warning exposure through ingredients such as botanicals, colors, and concentrates.

functions.label: Additive
functions.definition: General functional additive not captured by a more specific function. Used for GRAS-pathway and state GRAS-reporting obligations.

functions.label: Dough Conditioner
functions.definition: Strengthens or bleaches dough. Named in ingredient bans even though it is rare in beverages.
